chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Hilal al-Razi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about two men who fought while they were in the state of Ihram. He said, 'Glory be to Allah, what a bad thing they did.' I said, 'They have indeed done it, so what is obligatory upon them?' He said, 'Upon each one of them is the blood (diyah). And whoever pulls out his tooth while he is in Ihram, upon him is the blood (diyah), it has been narrated.

key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood money (diyah) payable as compensation or expiation
key_terms.ضِرْسَهُ: His tooth (specifically a molar or premolar)
key_terms.مُحْرِمَانِ: Two men in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for fighting or pulling out a tooth while in Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of 'dam' (blood money) is applied not only to physical combat but also to the specific act of plucking a tooth, illustrating the juristic principle that minor bodily alterations during Ihram incur the same financial penalty as major injuries. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the sanctity of the Ihram state, where even seemingly trivial actions are weighed against the spiritual discipline required during Hajj and Umrah. The ruling underscores the continuity of legal obligations from the Prophet's era through the Imams, reinforcing the detailed jurisprudence found in works like Tahdhib al-Ahkam.
